verses.text: That night the whole community cried out loudly, and the people wept.
All the people of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. The whole community said to them, "We wish we had died in Egypt, or even here in this desert!
Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, only to have us killed in battle? Our wives and children will be taken captive! Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
And they said to one another, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground in front of the whole community of Israel gathered there.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of the men who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole community of Israel, "The land we passed through and explored is a very, very good land.
If the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not turn against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land. We will swallow them up like bread. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!"
But the whole community talked about stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the people of Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people treat me with no respect? How long will they refuse to trust me, even after all the miracles I have done among them?
I will strike them with a deadly disease and destroy them. Then I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they are."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear about it! By your power you brought these people out from among them.

And they will tell the people who live in this land. They have already heard that you, LORD, are with these people, that you are seen face to face, that your cloud stays over them, and that you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you kill all these people at once, the nations who have heard about you will say,
'The LORD was not able to bring these people into the land he promised them, so he killed them in the desert.'
So now, Lord, please show how great your power is, just as you have said:

'The LORD is slow to become angry and full of faithful love. He forgives sin and rebellion. Yet he does not let the guilty go unpunished. He punishes children for the sins of their parents, to the third and fourth generation.'
Please forgive the sin of these people, because your faithful love is so great, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt until now."
The LORD answered, "I have forgiven them, as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD,
not one of these men will see the land. They saw my glory and the miracles I did in Egypt and in the desert, yet they have tested me ten times and have not obeyed me.
Not one of them will see the land I promised their ancestors. None of those who treated me with no respect will see it.
But my servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed me with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land he explored, and his descendants will own it.
Since the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and set out into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"How long must I put up with this evil community that complains against me? I have heard the complaints of the people of Israel against me.
So tell them: 'As surely as I live, says the LORD, I will do to you exactly what I heard you say.
Your dead bodies will fall in this desert. Every one of you twenty years old or more who was counted, who complained against me,
will never enter the land where I promised to settle you. Only Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun will enter it.
You said your children would be taken captive. But I will bring them in, and they will enjoy the land you have rejected.
But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this desert.
Your children will wander like shepherds in this desert for forty years. They will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the desert.
For forty years, one year for each of the forty days you explored the land, you will suffer for your sins. Then you will know what it is like to have me against you.'
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do these things to this whole evil community that has joined together against me. They will come to their end in this desert, and here they will die."
The men Moses had sent to explore the land came back and made the whole community complain against him by spreading a bad report about the land.
These men who spread the bad report about the land were struck down by a disease and died before the LORD.
Of all the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh stayed alive.
When Moses told all the people of Israel what the LORD had said, they were filled with sorrow.
Early the next morning they set out for the top of the hill country. They said, "We have sinned. Now we are ready to go to the place the LORD promised."
But Moses said, "Why are you disobeying the LORD's command? This will not succeed!
Do not go up, because the LORD is not with you. You will be beaten by your enemies.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will be killed in battle. Because you have turned away from following the LORD, he will not be with you."
But they dared to go up toward the top of the hill country anyway. Neither Moses nor the Covenant Box of the LORD left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and attacked them, and beat them all the way to Hormah.
